headline: Riding Mountain National Park Entry and Boat Inspection Requirements
reservation: Entry to Clear Lake requires a valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass or a daily admission fee, which must be purchased at the park gate. For those bringing watercraft, a mandatory Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) inspection and permit are required before launching; check the official Parks Canada site for current inspection station locations. Campsites and the historic park lodge require reservations months in advance through the national portal.

days.title: Wasagaming Waterfront and Boardwalks

stops.name: Wasagaming Main Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the clear, spring-fed waters and the iconic stone pier that characterizes this historic resort town.

stops.name: Ominibi Trail
stops.detail: Walk this gentle loop near the lake shore to see the transition from boreal forest to parkland meadows.

days.driving: Local walking or 10-minute drive; traffic in town is slow during summer.
days.note: Parking near the beach is highly limited; consider walking from your accommodation if staying in Wasagaming.

days.title: Bison and Boreal Heights

stops.name: Lake Audy Bison Enclosure
stops.detail: Drive through the prairie landscape to view the captive bison herd in their natural habitat.

stops.name: Bald Hill Trail
stops.detail: Hike toward the eastern escarpment for a rare view of the Manitoba lowlands from the 'mountain' peaks.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours round trip; Lake Audy Road is often unpaved gravel.
days.note: Check road conditions at the visitor center as rain can make the Lake Audy route slippery for small cars.

days.title: Deep Woods and Quiet Coves

stops.name: Frith Lake
stops.detail: Explore the quieter western reaches of the park for a contrast to the busy main beach area.

stops.name: Wishing Well
stops.detail: Visit the manicured English gardens at the park's historic core, featuring stone bridges and floral displays.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total; focus is on short transit between forest trailheads.
days.note: Black bear sightings are frequent in the western woods; maintain distance and follow park protocols.

intel.title: Wasagaming Townsite
intel.text: Parking is regulated and fills by 11 AM during peak July weekends. Use peripheral lots and be prepared for a 10-minute walk to the Clear Lake shoreline.

intel.title: Park-Wide Connectivity
intel.text: Reliable cell signal is found within Wasagaming and along Highway 10. Expect total signal loss when heading toward the Lake Audy or western backcountry areas.

intel.title: On-Site Services
intel.text: Fuel is available in Wasagaming and the nearby town of Onanole. Availability outside these hubs is non-existent within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Midsummer Peak
intel.text: July and August are the busiest months. Arriving at the park gate before 9 AM or after 4 PM helps avoid long vehicle queues on Highway 10.

intel.title: Watercraft Restrictions
intel.text: Clear Lake has strict AIS protocols to prevent Zebra Mussels. All boats, including kayaks, must be certified 'clean, drain, dry' by official staff.

plan.arrival: Fly into Brandon or Dauphin, pick up a rental, and drive toward the Highway 10 park entrance. Ensure you have your park pass before arriving at the townsite.
plan.vehicle: Sedans are fine for Wasagaming, but an SUV is preferred if you plan to explore the gravel roads leading to Lake Audy or the trailheads.
plan.goldenHour: The Wasagaming Pier is the premier location for sunset, where the sun dips directly over the western expanse of Clear Lake.
